docs.title: Aurastream
docs.text:
One endpoint. 26+ data sources. Zero infrastructure.

Aurastream is a unified financial data API. Instead of integrating with each exchange and data provider individually, make a single POST request to Aurastream and get OHLCV bars, trades, quotes, funding rates, economic indicators, and more.

docs.title: Why Aurastream?
docs.text: Without Aurastream With Aurastream Integrate each exchange API separately One POST request for all sources Manage rate limits, pagination, retries Handled server-side Run infrastructure to host data pipelines We host it for you Different response formats per provider Consistent {ticker: {timestamp: {OHLCV}}}

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
import requests

URL = "https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_AURASTREAM_API_KEY"}

response = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["BTCUSDT"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2025-01-31",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "bybit",
})

data = response.json()
# {"BTCUSDT": {"2025-01-01 00:00:00": {"Open": ..., "High": ..., ...}, ...}}

docs.title: Response Format
docs.text: All successful responses from the /timeseries endpoint return data in the same nested dictionary format, regardless of the data source.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: {ticker: {timestamp: {field: value}}}

docs.title: Single ticker
docs.text:
import pandas as pd

ticker = "EUR_USD"
df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(data[ticker], orient="index")
df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
df = df.astype(float).sort_index()

docs.title: Multiple tickers
docs.text:
frames = {}
for ticker, values in data.items():
    df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(values, orient="index")
    df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
    frames[ticker] = df.astype(float).sort_index()

# Access individual DataFrames
eur = frames["EUR_USD"]
gbp = frames["GBP_USD"]

docs.title: Multi-level DataFrame
docs.text:
panels = []
for ticker, values in data.items():
    df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(values, orient="index")
    df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
    df = df.astype(float).sort_index()
    df.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([[ticker], df.columns])
    panels.append(df)

combined = pd.concat(panels, axis=1)
# Access: combined["EUR_USD"]["Close"]

docs.title: Extracting a Single Field
docs.text:
To pull just the closing prices for plotting or analysis:

def to_series(data, ticker, field="Close"):
    ts = data[ticker]
    s = pd.Series({k: float(v[field]) for k, v in ts.items()})
    s.index = pd.to_datetime(s.index)
    return s.sort_index()

close = to_series(data, "EUR_USD", "Close")

docs.title: Empty Responses
docs.text:
If a ticker has no data for the requested range, its entry will be an empty dictionary:

{
    "INVALID_TICKER": {}
}

Check for this before processing:

if not data.get("INVALID_TICKER"):
    print("No data returned for this ticker")

docs.title: POST /timeseries
docs.text: Fetch historical time series data from any supported source.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: POST https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Required Description x-api-key Yes Your Aurastream API key Content-Type Yes application/json

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
{
    "tickerlist": ["BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2025-06-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "bybit",
    "credentials": null
}

docs.title: Core Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description tickerlist list[str] or null Yes — List of ticker symbols to fetch start str Yes — Start date in YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format end str Yes — End date in YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format interval str Yes — Bar interval (see Intervals) source str Yes — Data source identifier (see Data Sources) credentials dict or null No null Source-specific credentials (see Credentials)

docs.title: Source-Specific Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Used By Description dtype str Alpaca, CoinAPI, Oanda, City Index Data type: "bars", "trades", "quotes", "orderbook", "positionbook", "tick" price_type str Oanda "A" (ask), "B" (bid), "M" (mid) instrument str Binance, Deribit "spot" or "derivative" assetclass str FirstRate "stock", "etf", "futures", "fx", "options", "crypto" category str Bybit Category (e.g., "linear") bartype str TradeStation Bar type (e.g., "Minute") indicator str Trading Economics Economic indicator (e.g., "gdp") metric str Nemeton Metric type (e.g., "cumulative-depth", "depth-ratio") level int Nemeton Depth level (default: 1000) variables list[str] Open-Meteo Weather variables (e.g., ["temperature_2m"]) db str SDMX Database identifier (e.g., "BIS") l1 str SDMX Aggregation label (e.g., "CBRate") filters dict Nasdaq Data filters continuous_contracts bool FirstRate Use continuous contracts for futures quote str CoinGecko Quote currency (default: "usd")

docs.title: Intervals
docs.text:
Interval Meaning Examples 1s, 5s, 30s Seconds Bybit, Binance 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m Minutes Most sources 1h, 4h Hours Most sources 1d Daily All sources 1w Weekly Most sources 1M Monthly Some sources

Interval support varies by source

Not every source supports every interval. See individual data source pages for supported intervals.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Pythoncurl 
import requests

URL = "https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY"}

response = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["XAU_USD"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2025-06-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "oanda",
    "credentials": {
        "id": "YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID",
        "token": "YOUR_TOKEN",
        "environment": "practice"
    }
})

data = response.json()

curl -X POST https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "tickerlist": ["XAU_USD"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2025-06-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "oanda",
    "credentials": {
      "id": "YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID",
      "token": "YOUR_TOKEN",
      "environment": "practice"
    }
  }'

docs.title: Timeout
docs.text: Requests have a 120-second timeout. For large date ranges or many tickers, consider splitting into smaller requests.

docs.title: Central Bank Policy Rates
docs.text:
Compare policy rates across countries using SDMX (BIS data):

import requests
import pandas as pd

URL = "https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_AURASTREAM_API_KEY"}

payload = {
    "tickerlist": [
        "BIS,WS_CBPOL,1.0/D.US",
        "BIS,WS_CBPOL,1.0/D.GB",
        "BIS,WS_CBPOL,1.0/D.XM",
        "BIS,WS_CBPOL,1.0/D.JP"
    ],
    "start": "2020-01-01",
    "end": "2025-06-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "sdmx",
    "db": "BIS",
    "l1": "CBRate"
}

response = requests.post(URL, json=payload, headers=HEADERS)
data = response.json()

# Parse into a single DataFrame of rates
rates = {}
labels = {"D.US": "Fed Funds", "D.GB": "BoE", "D.XM": "ECB", "D.JP": "BoJ"}
for ticker, bars in data.items():
    df = pd.DataFrame(bars).T
    df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
    key = ticker.split("/")[-1]
    rates[labels.get(key, key)] = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(float)

rates_df = pd.DataFrame(rates).ffill()
print(rates_df.tail(10))

docs.title: Multi-Asset Dashboard
docs.text:
Pull everything together into a single analysis:

from datetime import datetime

START = "2024-06-01"
END = "2025-06-01"

def fetch(tickerlist, source, **kwargs):
    payload = {
        "tickerlist": tickerlist,
        "start": START, "end": END,
        "interval": "1d",
        "source": source,
        **kwargs,
    }
    resp = requests.post(URL, json=payload, headers=HEADERS)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    frames = {}
    for t, bars in resp.json().items():
        df = pd.DataFrame(bars).T
        df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
        df = df.astype(float)
        frames[t] = df
    return frames

# 1. Equities
equities = fetch(["SPY", "QQQ", "IWM"], "yahoo")

# 2. Crypto
crypto = fetch(["BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT"], "bybit")

# 3. Forex
fx = fetch(["EUR_USD", "GBP_USD"], "oanda",
           credentials={"id": "YOUR_ID", "token": "YOUR_TOKEN",
                        "environment": "practice"})

# 4. Macro
rates = fetch(
    ["BIS,WS_CBPOL,1.0/D.US", "BIS,WS_CBPOL,1.0/D.XM"],
    "sdmx", db="BIS", l1="CBRate"
)

# Combine closes
closes = pd.DataFrame({
    **{t: f["Close"] for t, f in equities.items()},
    **{t: f["Close"] for t, f in crypto.items()},
    **{t: f["Close"] for t, f in fx.items()},
})

# Normalize to 100
normalized = closes / closes.iloc[0] * 100
print(normalized.tail())

docs.title: Reusable Helper Function
docs.text:
def fetch(tickerlist, source, start, end, interval="1d",
          credentials=None, **kwargs):
    """Fetch data from Aurastream and return a dict of DataFrames."""
    payload = {
        "tickerlist": tickerlist,
        "start": start,
        "end": end,
        "interval": interval,
        "source": source,
        **kwargs,
    }
    if credentials:
        payload["credentials"] = credentials

    resp = requests.post(URL, json=payload, headers=HEADERS)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    result = {}
    for ticker, bars in resp.json().items():
        df = pd.DataFrame(bars).T
        df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
        df = df.astype(float)
        result[ticker] = df
    return result


# Usage
btc = fetch(["BTCUSDT"], "bybit", "2025-01-01", "2025-06-01")["BTCUSDT"]
print(btc.tail())

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

frames = fetch(["AAPL", "MSFT"], "yahoo", "2024-01-01", "2025-06-01")

docs.title: Combining Sources
docs.text:
Aurastream's unified format makes it easy to combine data from different sources:

# Equity prices from Yahoo
equities = fetch(["SPY"], "yahoo", "2024-01-01", "2025-06-01")

# Macro data from FRED
fred = fetch(
    ["USACPIALLMINMEI"],
    "fred",
    "2024-01-01",
    "2025-06-01",
    credentials={"key": "YOUR_FRED_KEY"}
)

# Both return the same {ticker: {timestamp: {fields}}} format
spy = equities["SPY"]
cpi = fred["USACPIALLMINMEI"]

print(f"SPY data points: {len(spy)}")
print(f"CPI data points: {len(cpi)}")

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Aurastream uses two layers of authentication:

  1. Aurastream API key — authenticates you against the Aurastream service
  2. Data source credentials — your own credentials for third-party data providers (when required)

docs.title: Aurastream API Key
docs.text:
Every request must include your Aurastream API key in the x-api-key header:

headers = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_AURASTREAM_API_KEY"}

You can find your API key in the Aurastream dashboard under API Keys.

Keep your API key secret

Never commit your API key to version control or share it publicly. Use environment variables or a secrets manager.

import os

headers = {"x-api-key": os.environ["AURASTREAM_API_KEY"]}

docs.title: Data Source Credentials
docs.text:
Some data sources require your own API credentials to access their data. These are passed in the credentials field of the request body — they are not stored on Aurastream servers.

response = requests.post(URL, headers=headers, json={
    "tickerlist": ["EUR_USD"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2025-06-01",
    "interval": "1h",
    "source": "oanda",
    "credentials": {
        "id": "YOUR_OANDA_ACCOUNT_ID",
        "token": "YOUR_OANDA_TOKEN",
        "environment": "practice"
    }
})

Credentials are never stored

Aurastream forwards your credentials directly to the upstream data source in real time. They are not saved, logged, or cached.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Get your first data in under 2 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An Aurastream API key (get one from the dashboard)
  • Python 3.8+ with requests installed, or any HTTP client

docs.title: 1. Install requests
docs.text: pip install requests

docs.title: 2. Make your first request
docs.text:
This example fetches daily Bitcoin data from Bybit (no exchange credentials needed):

import requests

URL = "https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_AURASTREAM_API_KEY"}

response = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["BTCUSDT"],
    "start": "2025-06-01",
    "end": "2025-06-30",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "bybit",
})

data = response.json()
print(data)

docs.title: 3. Parse the response
docs.text:
The response is a nested dictionary: {ticker: {timestamp: {OHLCV}}}.

import pandas as pd

ticker = "BTCUSDT"
df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(data[ticker], orient="index")
df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
df = df.sort_index()
df = df.astype(float)

print(df.head())

docs.title: 4. Try a source that requires credentials
docs.text:
Some sources (Oanda, Alpaca, etc.) require your own exchange credentials. Pass them in the request body:

response = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["EUR_USD", "GBP_USD"],
    "start": "2025-06-01",
    "end": "2025-06-30",
    "interval": "1h",
    "source": "oanda",
    "credentials": {
        "id": "YOUR_OANDA_ACCOUNT_ID",
        "token": "YOUR_OANDA_API_TOKEN",
        "environment": "practice"
